bottom_line: In ASCOT-LLA, atorvastatin 10 mg vs placebo reduced the primary endpoint (non-fatal MI plus fatal CHD) (hazard ratio 0.64 [0.50–0.83], p=0.0005).
implications: These results support that, over a median 3.3 years, atorvastatin 10 mg (vs placebo) was associated with fewer primary endpoint events (100 vs 154; hazard ratio 0.64 [0.50–0.83]) and fewer fatal/non-fatal strokes (89 vs 121; 0.73 [0.56–0.96]) in this hypertensive population. The trial does not show a statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (185 vs 212; 0.87 [0.71–1.06]) and provides limited safety signals based on reported serious adverse events and one rhabdomyolysis case.

criticisms.text: Trial stopped prematurely, shortening follow-up versus what was planned.
criticisms.quote:
The study was stopped prematurely after 33 041 patient-
 years of follow-up (median 3·3 years).

criticisms.text: The reduced follow-up and small number of events among patients with diabetes may have resulted in inadequate power for that subgroup analysis.
criticisms.quote:
the absolute number of events among patients
  with diabetes was only 84. This finding may well, therefore,
  reflect inadequate power, especially given the shortened
  follow-up period

criticisms.text: Potential shortcoming: mainly white male participants, limiting inference about women; small number of events among women.
criticisms.quote:
these results highlight a potential
  shortcoming of ASCOT which, in common with most
  previous large statin studies, included mainly white male
  participants.

criticisms.text: Interpretation should be tempered by the small absolute risk reduction reported.
criticisms.quote:
Reaction to the 36% relative reduction in the primary
 endpoint and the other benefits observed in ASCOT may
 need to be tempered by consideration of the absolute risk
 reduction of a coronary event of 3·4 per 1000 patient-years.

criticisms.text: Financial implications are noted for statin use in hypertensive patients at this level of absolute risk.
criticisms.quote:
Furthermore there are clearly financial implications of statin
 use among all hypertensive patients with absolute levels of
 cardiovascular risk as low as those included in ASCOT.
